# rind on pi2b-bench: Raspberry Pi 2 Model B (armv7 Cortex-A7)

Five rounds on a Raspberry Pi 2 Model B Rev 1.1 (BCM2836, four Cortex-A7 cores at 900 MHz, NEON, no ARMv8 cryptography extensions) at [kixel-ai/rind `a6577cb4`](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/commit/a6577cb4a4b48af06385f8d748f3892c07cc229e), on 2026-11-13 from 10:24 AM to 1:05 PM America/Los_Angeles (board clock 13:24:02 to 16:05:32 UTC-5).

The binaries were the rind-bench criterion harnesses, cross-compiled for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`. This set was not produced by `admin/bench-report run`. Each published time is the median of the five rounds' criterion estimates (`pi2b-bench.json`, schema 1, each run's estimate in `runs_ns`). [RUNS.md](RUNS.md) lists every run, [facts.txt](facts.txt) the hardware, and [NOTES.md](NOTES.md) how the board was run.

- Board: Raspberry Pi 2 Model B Rev 1.1, 920 MiB visible (1 GB board)
- CPU: ARMv7 Processor rev 5 (v7l), armv7l, 4 logical CPUs, 900 MHz, governor `performance` during the rounds
- OS: Raspbian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) (Linux 6.18.60+rpt-rpi-v7)
- Toolchain: rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01), cargo 1.98.1; cross-built on macOS with clang 22, rust-lld and the Pi sysroot
- OpenSSL linked: OpenSSL 3.5.9 29 Sep 2026 (the Pi's system library)
- Libraries: rind, aws-lc-rs, ring, RustCrypto, libcrux, OpenSSL. Graviola was not built (x86_64/aarch64 only).
- rind-cpuid: no armv7 output. rind's NEON path was confirmed by `detects_the_expected_cpu`.
- Criterion: `--noplot --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 3 --sample-size 10`
- Pin: cpu3. lightdm and gpsd were stopped. The board was otherwise idle. No run was flagged noisy.
- Thermal: 42.2–46.0 °C, `throttled=0x0`, clock 900 MHz in every round
- `build_cost`: not measured (the binaries were cross-compiled on another host)

Of the 68 operations, rind was fastest on 38, aws-lc-rs on 20, OpenSSL on 6, ring on 2, and RustCrypto on 2. libcrux was fastest on none. A tie counts for rind, which is the same rule `cargo verify` uses.

## Method and validation

Validation ran on the board at the same commit, using the `sh/armv7.sh` matrix. Doctests were not run (the tests were cross-compiled).

- NEON enabled: 1023 passed, 0 failed, 34 ignored
- NEON denied (`RIND_CPU_DISABLE_neon`): 1023 passed, 0 failed, 34 ignored
- Memory-wipe tests, both modes: 28 passed, 0 failed
- `detects_the_expected_cpu` passed in both tiers

Harness order rotated each round. After the last round the governor was restored to `ondemand` and lightdm and gpsd were started again.

Round 5 of `mldsa65-sign` for OpenSSL was 20.46 ms. The other four rounds were 17.32, 18.01, 18.19 and 18.41 ms (median of those four: 18.10 ms). The published OpenSSL figure is the median of all five, 18.19 ms, so that every operation and library appears in every run and the host JSON matches the median `cargo verify` recomputes. No other pair was treated as a spike. All five rounds are valid.

## Gaps

Each operation where another library is more than 10% faster than rind, by rind's rule (OpenSSL counts), with its reason from [gaps.toml](gaps.toml). `cargo xtask host-report` refuses a gap without an entry and an entry that covers no gap.

| Operations | rind over the fastest | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `rustls-bulk/aes128-gcm`, `rustls-bulk/aes256-gcm`, `aes128-gcm/32B`, `aes128-gcm/1350B`, `aes128-gcm/16KB`, `aes128-gcm-open/32B`, `aes128-gcm-open/1350B`, `aes128-gcm-open/16KB`, `aes256-gcm/32B`, `aes256-gcm/1350B`, `aes256-gcm/16KB`, `aes256-gcm-open/32B`, `aes256-gcm-open/1350B`, `aes256-gcm-open/16KB` | 3.71× aws-lc-rs; 3.71× aws-lc-rs; 3.22× aws-lc-rs; 3.82× aws-lc-rs; 3.91× aws-lc-rs; 3.16× aws-lc-rs; 3.80× aws-lc-rs; 3.89× aws-lc-rs; 3.33× aws-lc-rs; 3.79× aws-lc-rs; 3.87× ring; 3.26× aws-lc-rs; 3.78× aws-lc-rs; 3.85× aws-lc-rs | The Cortex-A7 has NEON but no AES instructions. aws-lc-rs and ring use ARMv7 NEON bitsliced AES (bsaes) and NEON GHASH (vmull.p8). rind is on a portable path here and matches RustCrypto. The same gap shows up in rustls bulk AES-GCM. |
| `quic-header-protection/aes128`, `quic-header-protection/aes256` | 5.13× aws-lc-rs; 5.28× aws-lc-rs | Header protection encrypts one AES block per packet. aws-lc-rs and ring have a faster single-block AES on this core; rind uses its portable path. This is separate from the bulk AES-CTR gap above. |
| `chacha20poly1305/32B` | 1.33× RustCrypto + dalek | Per-call setup (key and nonce init, Poly1305 key generation) is a larger share of a 32-byte message. RustCrypto is fastest at this size. |
| `chacha20poly1305/16KB` | 1.12× OpenSSL | OpenSSL's NEON ChaCha uses a wider interleave than rind's on this armv7 core. |
| `xchacha20poly1305/32B` | 1.26× RustCrypto + dalek | The same per-call setup cost as ChaCha20-Poly1305 at 32 B. RustCrypto is fastest at this size. |
| `p256-ecdh`, `p256-ecdsa-verify` | 1.11× OpenSSL; 1.19× OpenSSL | OpenSSL's 32-bit ARM ecp_nistz256 Montgomery assembly is ahead. rind is still faster than aws-lc-rs, ring, RustCrypto and libcrux on these rows. |
| `p521-ecdsa-verify` | 1.15× aws-lc-rs | aws-lc-rs is slightly ahead on the P-521 verify path. |

## Also behind, but under 10%

These are slower than the fastest other library, but not gaps by rind's 10% rule. Numbers are the same medians as the tables above.

- P-256 ECDSA-sign is 1.08× behind OpenSSL (1.11 ms vs 1.03 ms).
- RSA-2048 PKCS#1 and PSS verify are 1.05× behind aws-lc-rs (752.94 µs vs 718.51 µs, and 781.55 µs vs 746.98 µs).
- rustls bulk ChaCha20-Poly1305 is 1.05× behind OpenSSL (54.15 ms vs 51.60 ms).
- Mid-size ChaCha20 and XChaCha20 rows are ties or within 2%.

On the other operations rind is already the fastest or tied, including the rustls full and resumed handshakes, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SHA-3, and P-384.
